Creation.TraitsInstructions: Write one evocative word for each, something that can enrich your character’s story.
Creation.VirtueGuidance: Choose one word that is more likely to solve problems than create them.
Creation.ViceGuidance: Choose one word that is more likely to create problems than solve them.
Creation.VirtueExamples: Examples: Adaptable · Brave · Caring · Clever · Generous · Honest · Hopeful · Patient · Resourceful · Steadfast
Creation.ViceExamples: Examples: Angry · Arrogant · Bossy · Cowardly · Greedy · Impulsive · Jealous · Reckless · Selfish · Stubborn
Creation.BothTraitsRequired: Write both a Virtue and a Vice before confirming.
Creation.NoIntroduction: The Gamemaster has not written the opening situation yet.
Creation.ConceptInstructions: Give your Survivor a name, a few visible details, and a brief idea of who they are. A profession or social position shapes the fiction but grants no mechanical bonus.
Creation.LookPlaceholder: Rain-soaked coat, tired eyes, a wedding ring worn on a chain.
Creation.ConceptPlaceholder: A paramedic who keeps moving because stopping means remembering.
Creation.ConceptRequired: Write a name, a look, and a concept before confirming.
Creation.MomentInstructions: Complete the thought: I will find hope when… This is a personal scene your Survivor longs to reach.
Creation.MomentGuidance: Make it specific, attainable, and powerful enough to deserve a scene. It must also carry a real possibility of failure.
Creation.MomentExamples: Examples: I bring my sister home · I hear my father forgive me · I see the ocean one last time · I make the children laugh again · I tell Mara the truth · I save someone I once abandoned · I finish the song we started · I prove there is still kindness in us
Creation.BrinkInstructions: Complete the thought: I have seen you… Secretly write what you discovered about {player}.
Creation.BrinkGuidance: Describe what they may become at their most desperate—not who they already are. Threaten their humanity, sanity, reliability, or the group's trust.
Creation.BrinkExamples: Examples: abandon someone who trusted you · smile while another person suffered · choose the mission over a human life · speak to someone who was not there · hide the last food from the group · leave a wounded friend behind · enjoy the power fear gave you · insist the voices knew the safest path
Creation.ThemBrinkInstructions: Complete the thought: I have seen Them… Secretly write one impossible and terrifying thing your Survivor personally witnessed Them do.
Creation.ThemBrinkGuidance: Reveal a concrete truth about how They hunt, move, imitate, or alter the world. Make it usable in the fiction without explaining Their origin or giving Them a certain weakness.
Creation.ThemBrinkExamples: Examples: walk across the ceiling without making a sound · wear the face of someone who vanished · call out in the exact voice of a dead loved one · pass through a door that had never opened · step from one shadow into another · know a memory no one had shared · stand motionless among the flames · smile with far too many teeth
Creation.ConfirmBrink: This is what I have seen
Creation.GmBrinkEyebrow: Your part in what we have seen
Creation.GmBrinkInstructions: Complete ‘I have seen you…’ for {player}. Write a dark possibility this Survivor might reach in desperation, not merely a flaw they already possess.
Creation.CardsHavePassed: The cards move around the table
Creation.NotTheCardsYouWrote: These are the truths you have inherited
Creation.DistributionNarrative: Keep your Moment. Your other cards now come from the people beside you. Read them before deciding who your Survivor is.
Creation.DistributionVirtue: Your Virtue was written by the participant on your left.
Creation.DistributionVice: Your Vice was written by the participant on your right.
Creation.DistributionBrink: Your Brink comes from the participant—or Gamemaster—on your right.
Creation.FinalizationInstruction: Now name your Survivor, describe their look and concept, record only what is truly in their pockets, arrange the three visible cards, and leave the Brink at the bottom before confirming everything.
Creation.FinalizationCompleteInstruction: Your Survivor is confirmed. You may reopen their sheet if you want to review or edit it.
Creation.OpenMySurvivor: Open my Survivor and finish them
Creation.FinalizationSheetGuide: Use the cards you received to decide who this person is. Complete every field, arrange the stack, lock it, then confirm the finished Survivor.
Creation.FinalizationIncomplete: Complete the name, look, concept, and inventory, then arrange and lock all four cards before confirming.
Creation.GmBrinkRequired: Write the Brink before saving it.

DebugMode.Hint: Log technical game data to the browser console, including candle lifetimes and every minute-by-minute risk check.

CandleClock.Title: The physical table
CandleClock.Hint: This setting only changes the accident risk. Burning is automatic: each candle naturally lasts 180 to 300 minutes of active play. Offline time and pauses—including Foundry, Consent Form, and X-Card pauses—do not count. Any extinction is final and immediately ends the current scene.

gale.Name: Strong wind — high chance
gale.Description: Accidental extinction chance: 2.5% per lit candle per minute of active play, 12.5 times the living room risk.

convention.Name: Convention — medium chance
convention.Description: Accidental extinction chance: 0.8% per lit candle per minute of active play, 4 times the living room risk.

livingRoom.Name: Living room — low chance (default)
livingRoom.Description: Accidental extinction chance: 0.2% per lit candle per minute of active play.

none.Name: None — natural lifetime only
none.Description: No accidental extinctions. Candles go out when their burn time ends or as required by the game rules.

CandleClock.Accident: A flame suddenly goes out. The scene ends immediately.
CandleClock.BurnedOut: A candle has reached the end of its life. The scene ends immediately.
CandleClock.PreparationExtinction: A flame has gone out during preparation. It remains dark, preparation continues, and one die passes permanently to the GM.
CandleClock.FinalFlame: The final flame dies on its own. Darkness takes everyone who remains.
CandleClock.Locked: This setting has been locked since the Game began.

Recording.Title: Leave a message behind
Recording.Introduction: Before you leave this place, the recorder passes around the table. Each Survivor leaves a brief message for anyone who may come looking after you are gone.
Recording.YourTurn: The recorder is in your hands
Recording.Prompt: What does your Survivor leave behind: who you are, what happened here, where you are going, a warning, a request for help, or a promise?
Recording.PassWarning: You will leave no message. Pass your turn?
Recording.RetakeWarning: Your current message will be replaced when you confirm the new take. Record it again?
Recording.RetakeExplanation: The recorder will return to you after its first trip around the table. Your current message remains safely stored until you confirm a new take.
Recording.OrUpload: No microphone? Choose an audio file
Recording.InvalidAudio: This file is not a valid, playable audio recording (50 MB maximum). It was not selected.
Recording.Consent: Recording begins only when you press the button. Confirming uploads this message to the Foundry server for this game.
Recording.Seal: Take back the recorder and begin Scene 1
